Who We Are

Big Build Construction is a licensed, bonded, and insured remodeling company specializing in kitchen remodeling, bathroom remodeling, and full home renovations across King, Pierce, and Snohomish counties. Founded by Oleg Nikityuk, we've built our reputation on delivering quality craftsmanship, transparent pricing, and reliable project timelines to homeowners throughout the greater Seattle area — including Kent, Auburn, Renton, Tukwila, Federal Way, and beyond.

With over 15 years of remodeling experience, we handle every phase of your project — from custom tile installation and LVP flooring to drywall finishing, trim carpentry, and complete interior renovations. You get one point of contact, clear communication, and no surprise change orders. Every quote is fixed-price and in writing before work begins.

Why Homeowners Choose Us

Hiring a remodeling contractor is a big decision. Most homeowners aren't worried about picking tile — they're worried about hiring someone who disappears mid-project, leaves dust through the house, or hits them with unexpected costs halfway through. That's the problem we solve.

Every project is managed directly by the owner. You get one point of contact from consultation through final walkthrough, clean job sites daily, and a structured process designed to keep your remodel on time and on budget. We're 5-star rated across Google, Facebook, and Yelp — not because we ask for reviews, but because our clients are genuinely happy with the result.

Whether you need a full kitchen renovation, a bathroom remodel with custom tile and a walk-in shower, LVP flooring installed throughout your home, or drywall and carpentry finishing — Big Build Construction delivers professional results backed by real accountability. Licensed, bonded, and insured, and trusted by homeowners across Western Washington.

MORE ABOUT US
Kitchen Remodeling That Changes How You Live

The kitchen is where most of our clients want to start — and for good reason. It's the highest-impact room in any home. Our kitchen remodeling projects cover everything from targeted upgrades like new quartz countertops, soft-close cabinetry, and modern lighting to full-scale open-concept transformations that completely reimagine the layout and flow of your space.

Homeowners across Seattle, Bellevue, Kent, and Tacoma are asking for oversized islands with built-in seating, concealed pantry storage, undermount sinks, and commercial-style ventilation. Whether you're working with an outdated galley kitchen from the '80s or a builder-grade layout that just feels generic, we design around how your family actually uses the space — not a one-size-fits-all template.

Most of our kitchen remodels run 6–10 weeks depending on scope, material lead times, and permit schedules. Every project gets a fixed-price written estimate before we start, so there's never a surprise halfway through.

SEE KITCHEN REMODELING
Bathroom Remodeling Built Around Your Lifestyle

A bathroom remodel can be as straightforward as replacing a dated vanity and re-tiling the shower surround, or as involved as reconfiguring plumbing to add a freestanding soaking tub, walk-in rain shower with frameless glass, and heated flooring throughout. Our bathroom remodeling team handles both — and everything in between.

We also do a lot of accessibility-focused work: curbless showers, grab bars that blend into the design, comfort-height toilets, and wider doorways. These modifications let homeowners age in place without sacrificing the look or feel of the space — something that matters more and more to families across King, Pierce, and Snohomish counties.

Typical bathroom remodels take 3–6 weeks, with material options ranging from porcelain and ceramic tile to natural stone, custom glass enclosures, and premium fixtures. As with every project, you get a fixed-price quote in writing before any work begins.

SEE BATHROOM REMODELING
Whole-Home Remodeling — When It's More Than One Room

Sometimes the project isn't limited to a single space. If your home feels disconnected, outdated, or cramped, a whole-home remodel lets you address layout, finishes, and flow all at once. We've taken 1970s split-levels and turned them into open, light-filled living spaces. We've modernized ramblers in Kent, updated homes in Renton, refreshed layouts in Federal Way, and transformed interiors across Bellevue, Tacoma, and beyond — each one tailored to how the homeowner actually lives.

Our whole-home projects typically involve new LVP or hardwood flooring throughout, drywall repair and finishing, custom tile in wet areas, trim and baseboard carpentry, fresh paint, and updated fixtures. The result is a home that looks better, functions better, and feels like it was designed around you — not the previous owner. One point of contact, from start to finish.

What Goes Into a Professional Kitchen Remodel

A kitchen remodel is more than swapping cabinets and counters. Every project we run moves through five phases: design and material selection, permit pull and demo, plumbing and electrical rough-in, cabinet and counter installation, and finish carpentry, tile, lighting, and inspection. Plumbing and electrical changes typically require a City permit and at least one rough-in inspection before walls close up, so we sequence the work to keep your schedule on track. Older homes often need supply line replacement, panel upgrades, or load-bearing rework once the cabinets come down — and we flag every one of those in writing the moment we find it, so there are no surprise invoices.

Cabinets typically lead time 4–8 weeks for semi-custom and 8–14 weeks for fully custom, which is why we lock in selections before demo begins. Countertops template after cabinets are set, then run 1–2 weeks at the fabricator. Knowing that sequence is half the battle — it's why our kitchen remodels stay on the written schedule we hand you at kickoff, instead of dragging out the way unmanaged projects often do.

Choosing Kitchen Materials That Hold Up

Quartz remains the most popular kitchen counter material in Western Washington for good reason — it resists stains, doesn't need sealing, and handles the heat and acidity of a working kitchen. Natural stone (granite, marble, soapstone) brings character but requires annual sealing and care around acidic foods. Solid-wood shaker cabinetry with soft-close hinges holds value long after trends shift, and panel-ready appliances integrate cleanly with the cabinet face for a flush look. For flooring, LVP and engineered hardwood both perform well in kitchens; full hardwood demands sealed seams and a vigilant homeowner.

We help homeowners choose between mid-range and premium tiers at every line item — cabinet brand, counter slab, faucet, range hood, lighting plan — and lay out the cost and durability trade-offs in writing. Most of our Western Washington kitchen clients land in the mid-to-upper range because the materials we recommend cost slightly more upfront but pay off in fewer service calls over a 10–15 year horizon.

What Goes Into a Professional Bathroom Remodel

Bathrooms are the hardest room in the house to remodel — and the most expensive per square foot — because of plumbing, electrical, ventilation, and waterproofing all crowded into a small space. A real bathroom remodel moves through design and fixture selection, demo down to the studs, plumbing reroute and electrical rework, waterproof membrane and substrate, tile, vanity, glass, and trim, and final fixtures and inspection. Cutting any of those phases — especially waterproofing — is how cheap bathroom remodels turn into expensive mold problems three years later.

Most Western Washington bathrooms benefit from rerouting the vent stack, upsizing the bath fan to a humidity-sensing unit, and replacing the original copper or galvanized supply lines with modern PEX while the walls are open. These behind-the-wall upgrades aren't optional in our climate — we live in one of the wettest, longest-shoulder-season environments in the country, and bathrooms take the brunt of it.

Built for Daily Moisture and Long-Term Use

Porcelain tile outperforms ceramic in wet areas because of its lower absorption rate and harder finish — a critical detail for curbless showers and bathroom floors. Natural stone (marble, travertine) brings character but requires sealing every 12–18 months and isn't recommended for steam showers. Frameless glass enclosures use 3/8" or 1/2" tempered glass with stainless or solid-brass hardware; we avoid the bargain hardware that pits within two seasons of Pacific Northwest humidity.

Fixtures matter more than most homeowners realize. Cartridge-based shower valves from Moen, Delta, and Kohler offer decades of replaceable parts; the cheaper compression valves common in builder-grade bathrooms typically fail within 7–10 years. We help you choose where to invest (waterproofing, plumbing, the shower valve) and where to save (decorative fittings you can swap in five years without opening walls).

Home Renovation Projects
What Goes Into a Full Home Renovation

A whole-home remodel is fundamentally different from a single-room project. Instead of one trade sequence, you're orchestrating four or five — structural changes, electrical and plumbing reroutes, HVAC modifications, multi-room demo and rebuild, and finish carpentry across the entire footprint — under one schedule. Done well, it's the cleanest way to update a home because every system aligns: new flooring runs continuous across rooms, wiring is brought up to current code in one pass, and the design language stays consistent room-to-room. Done badly, it's the kind of project that drags 18+ months and leaves families living in dust.

The most common whole-home scopes we run combine a kitchen remodel, two or more bathroom remodels, and full-house flooring with paint and trim. Larger projects add wall removals for open-concept living, master suite expansions, and finished basements or ADUs. Every project starts with structural review (load paths, beam sizing, header detailing), an electrical load calculation against the existing panel, and a written week-by-week schedule organized so trades don't trip over each other.

Living Through the Remodel — How We Keep It Manageable

Most homeowners stay in the house during a whole-home renovation, which means sequencing matters more than scope. We zone the work — typically kitchens and primary baths get done first while a secondary kitchen or bathroom stays operational — and seal off active work areas with dust walls and HEPA filtration. Daily cleanup is non-negotiable on our jobs, because we know the homeowner is sleeping 30 feet from where we're cutting drywall the next morning.

Communication is the other half of the equation. Every project gets a shared schedule with milestones, a single point of contact (the owner, not a project manager who's juggling 12 jobs), and same-day responses to questions. Surprises behind the wall happen on every remodel — knob-and-tube, hidden rot, undersized plumbing — and we surface them in writing the moment we find them, with cost and timeline impact, so you can decide before we keep going.

What Goes Into a Professional Kitchen Remodel

A kitchen remodel is more than swapping cabinets and counters. Every project we run moves through five phases: design and material selection, permit pull and demo, plumbing and electrical rough-in, cabinet and counter installation, and finish carpentry, tile, lighting, and inspection. Plumbing and electrical changes typically require a City permit and at least one rough-in inspection before walls close up, so we sequence the work to keep your schedule on track. Older homes often need supply line replacement, panel upgrades, or load-bearing rework once the cabinets come down — and we flag every one of those in writing the moment we find it, so there are no surprise invoices.

Cabinets typically lead time 4–8 weeks for semi-custom and 8–14 weeks for fully custom, which is why we lock in selections before demo begins. Countertops template after cabinets are set, then run 1–2 weeks at the fabricator. Knowing that sequence is half the battle — it's why our kitchen remodels stay on the written schedule we hand you at kickoff, instead of dragging out the way unmanaged projects often do.

Choosing Kitchen Materials That Hold Up

Quartz remains the most popular kitchen counter material in Western Washington for good reason — it resists stains, doesn't need sealing, and handles the heat and acidity of a working kitchen. Natural stone (granite, marble, soapstone) brings character but requires annual sealing and care around acidic foods. Solid-wood shaker cabinetry with soft-close hinges holds value long after trends shift, and panel-ready appliances integrate cleanly with the cabinet face for a flush look. For flooring, LVP and engineered hardwood both perform well in kitchens; full hardwood demands sealed seams and a vigilant homeowner.

We help homeowners choose between mid-range and premium tiers at every line item — cabinet brand, counter slab, faucet, range hood, lighting plan — and lay out the cost and durability trade-offs in writing. Most of our Western Washington kitchen clients land in the mid-to-upper range because the materials we recommend cost slightly more upfront but pay off in fewer service calls over a 10–15 year horizon.

How much does a kitchen remodel cost in Seattle?
Kitchen remodeling costs in Seattle typically range from $15,000 for a cosmetic update to $75,000+ for a full custom kitchen renovation. Costs depend on scope, materials, cabinetry style, countertop choice, appliances, and whether layout changes require plumbing or electrical work. We provide detailed, transparent estimates during your free consultation.
How long does a kitchen remodel take?
Most kitchen remodels take 4–8 weeks depending on scope. Cosmetic updates (new paint, backsplash, hardware) may take 2–3 weeks. Full gut renovations with structural changes, new plumbing, or electrical work can take 8–12 weeks. We provide a detailed timeline upfront and communicate any changes immediately.
Can you handle custom kitchen design?

What Goes Into a Professional Bathroom Remodel

Bathrooms are the hardest room in the house to remodel — and the most expensive per square foot — because of plumbing, electrical, ventilation, and waterproofing all crowded into a small space. A real bathroom remodel moves through design and fixture selection, demo down to the studs, plumbing reroute and electrical rework, waterproof membrane and substrate, tile, vanity, glass, and trim, and final fixtures and inspection. Cutting any of those phases — especially waterproofing — is how cheap bathroom remodels turn into expensive mold problems three years later.

Most Western Washington bathrooms benefit from rerouting the vent stack, upsizing the bath fan to a humidity-sensing unit, and replacing the original copper or galvanized supply lines with modern PEX while the walls are open. These behind-the-wall upgrades aren't optional in our climate — we live in one of the wettest, longest-shoulder-season environments in the country, and bathrooms take the brunt of it.

Built for Daily Moisture and Long-Term Use

Porcelain tile outperforms ceramic in wet areas because of its lower absorption rate and harder finish — a critical detail for curbless showers and bathroom floors. Natural stone (marble, travertine) brings character but requires sealing every 12–18 months and isn't recommended for steam showers. Frameless glass enclosures use 3/8" or 1/2" tempered glass with stainless or solid-brass hardware; we avoid the bargain hardware that pits within two seasons of Pacific Northwest humidity.

Fixtures matter more than most homeowners realize. Cartridge-based shower valves from Moen, Delta, and Kohler offer decades of replaceable parts; the cheaper compression valves common in builder-grade bathrooms typically fail within 7–10 years. We help you choose where to invest (waterproofing, plumbing, the shower valve) and where to save (decorative fittings you can swap in five years without opening walls).

OUR WORK

Home Renovation Projects
What Goes Into a Full Home Renovation

A whole-home remodel is fundamentally different from a single-room project. Instead of one trade sequence, you're orchestrating four or five — structural changes, electrical and plumbing reroutes, HVAC modifications, multi-room demo and rebuild, and finish carpentry across the entire footprint — under one schedule. Done well, it's the cleanest way to update a home because every system aligns: new flooring runs continuous across rooms, wiring is brought up to current code in one pass, and the design language stays consistent room-to-room. Done badly, it's the kind of project that drags 18+ months and leaves families living in dust.

The most common whole-home scopes we run combine a kitchen remodel, two or more bathroom remodels, and full-house flooring with paint and trim. Larger projects add wall removals for open-concept living, master suite expansions, and finished basements or ADUs. Every project starts with structural review (load paths, beam sizing, header detailing), an electrical load calculation against the existing panel, and a written week-by-week schedule organized so trades don't trip over each other.

Living Through the Remodel — How We Keep It Manageable

Most homeowners stay in the house during a whole-home renovation, which means sequencing matters more than scope. We zone the work — typically kitchens and primary baths get done first while a secondary kitchen or bathroom stays operational — and seal off active work areas with dust walls and HEPA filtration. Daily cleanup is non-negotiable on our jobs, because we know the homeowner is sleeping 30 feet from where we're cutting drywall the next morning.

Communication is the other half of the equation. Every project gets a shared schedule with milestones, a single point of contact (the owner, not a project manager who's juggling 12 jobs), and same-day responses to questions. Surprises behind the wall happen on every remodel — knob-and-tube, hidden rot, undersized plumbing — and we surface them in writing the moment we find them, with cost and timeline impact, so you can decide before we keep going.

Who We Are

Big Build Construction is a licensed, bonded, and insured remodeling company specializing in kitchen remodeling, bathroom remodeling, and full home renovations across King, Pierce, and Snohomish counties. Founded by Oleg Nikityuk, we've built our reputation on delivering quality craftsmanship, transparent pricing, and reliable project timelines to homeowners throughout the greater Seattle area — including Kent, Auburn, Renton, Tukwila, Federal Way, and beyond.

With over 15 years of remodeling experience, we handle every phase of your project — from custom tile installation and LVP flooring to drywall finishing, trim carpentry, and complete interior renovations. You get one point of contact, clear communication, and no surprise change orders. Every quote is fixed-price and in writing before work begins.

Why Homeowners Choose Us

Hiring a remodeling contractor is a big decision. Most homeowners aren't worried about picking tile — they're worried about hiring someone who disappears mid-project, leaves dust through the house, or hits them with unexpected costs halfway through. That's the problem we solve.

Every project is managed directly by the owner. You get one point of contact from consultation through final walkthrough, clean job sites daily, and a structured process designed to keep your remodel on time and on budget. We're 5-star rated across Google, Facebook, and Yelp — not because we ask for reviews, but because our clients are genuinely happy with the result.

Whether you need a full kitchen renovation, a bathroom remodel with custom tile and a walk-in shower, LVP flooring installed throughout your home, or drywall and carpentry finishing — Big Build Construction delivers professional results backed by real accountability. Licensed, bonded, and insured, and trusted by homeowners across Western Washington.

MORE ABOUT US
Kitchen Remodeling That Changes How You Live

The kitchen is where most of our clients want to start — and for good reason. It's the highest-impact room in any home. Our kitchen remodeling projects cover everything from targeted upgrades like new quartz countertops, soft-close cabinetry, and modern lighting to full-scale open-concept transformations that completely reimagine the layout and flow of your space.

Homeowners across Seattle, Bellevue, Kent, and Tacoma are asking for oversized islands with built-in seating, concealed pantry storage, undermount sinks, and commercial-style ventilation. Whether you're working with an outdated galley kitchen from the '80s or a builder-grade layout that just feels generic, we design around how your family actually uses the space — not a one-size-fits-all template.

Most of our kitchen remodels run 6–10 weeks depending on scope, material lead times, and permit schedules. Every project gets a fixed-price written estimate before we start, so there's never a surprise halfway through.

SEE KITCHEN REMODELING
Bathroom Remodeling Built Around Your Lifestyle

A bathroom remodel can be as straightforward as replacing a dated vanity and re-tiling the shower surround, or as involved as reconfiguring plumbing to add a freestanding soaking tub, walk-in rain shower with frameless glass, and heated flooring throughout. Our bathroom remodeling team handles both — and everything in between.

We also do a lot of accessibility-focused work: curbless showers, grab bars that blend into the design, comfort-height toilets, and wider doorways. These modifications let homeowners age in place without sacrificing the look or feel of the space — something that matters more and more to families across King, Pierce, and Snohomish counties.

Typical bathroom remodels take 3–6 weeks, with material options ranging from porcelain and ceramic tile to natural stone, custom glass enclosures, and premium fixtures. As with every project, you get a fixed-price quote in writing before any work begins.

SEE BATHROOM REMODELING
Whole-Home Remodeling — When It's More Than One Room

Sometimes the project isn't limited to a single space. If your home feels disconnected, outdated, or cramped, a whole-home remodel lets you address layout, finishes, and flow all at once. We've taken 1970s split-levels and turned them into open, light-filled living spaces. We've modernized ramblers in Kent, updated homes in Renton, refreshed layouts in Federal Way, and transformed interiors across Bellevue, Tacoma, and beyond — each one tailored to how the homeowner actually lives.

Our whole-home projects typically involve new LVP or hardwood flooring throughout, drywall repair and finishing, custom tile in wet areas, trim and baseboard carpentry, fresh paint, and updated fixtures. The result is a home that looks better, functions better, and feels like it was designed around you — not the previous owner. One point of contact, from start to finish.

Maintaining readable text and color contrast

Kitchen Remodelers Who Know How Auburn Houses Were Built

In Auburn, the age of the house sets half the kitchen scope before anyone picks a countertop. The 1950s-through-1970s ranches and split-levels around downtown and North Auburn tend to hide undersized supply lines, original 2-wire feeds behind the range, and load-bearing walls that block the open island layout everyone asks for first. Out in the 1990s–2000s Lakeland Hills and Lea Hill subdivisions the bones are sound — engineered floor trusses, modern panels — so the budget shifts toward tearing out builder-grade cabinets and laminate instead of repairing systems.

Our company is based in Kent, a 12–15 minute run down West Valley Highway or up Highway 167, which means we're on Auburn kitchens almost daily for measurements, cabinet deliveries, and inspection sign-offs. AUBURN PERMITS & CONSIDERATIONS

Auburn Kitchen Permits, Without the Guesswork

Auburn's building department wants a permit the moment a kitchen job crosses into structural changes, electrical alterations, plumbing relocation, or gas line work. Swapping cabinet doors, painting, or dropping new countertops onto the existing plumbing usually stays permit-free — but relocate the sink or run a fresh circuit for the range and you're firmly in permit territory.

We file through the Auburn Permit Center, line up the rough-in and final inspections, and hand you the closed permit record for your files. It's cheap insurance: unpermitted kitchen work is exactly what stalls a sale once a buyer's inspector starts asking questions.

Applications submitted to the City of Auburn on our contractor license, not the homeowner's

Lakeland Hills HOA familiarity — we flag the design changes that need board sign-off

HONEST PRICING

What Auburn Homeowners Actually Spend on a Kitchen

Auburn kitchens sit mid-range for the Puget Sound area. The bands below are what we see on real local jobs — your figure comes down to kitchen size, how far the scope reaches, and the finishes you choose, and it's all itemized before anything gets ordered.

REFRESH
$20,000 – $32,000

Cabinet refacing or paint, new countertops, sink & faucet swap, backsplash, and updated lighting. Same footprint, no moving plumbing.

MID-RANGE REMODEL
$32,000 – $50,000

New stock or semi-custom cabinets, quartz counters, new appliances, flooring, lighting, and minor electrical/plumbing updates. The most common project here.

FULL CUSTOM
$50,000 – $65,000+

Custom cabinetry, layout changes, wall removal, premium appliances, panel upgrades, and high-end finishes.

These are typical Auburn kitchen figures and exclude the surprises we can't see until demo — rot under the sink base, knob-and-tube behind a wall, a soft subfloor. When we find them, you get it in writing that day, never tucked quietly into the final invoice.

AUBURN KITCHEN REMODEL FAQS

What Auburn Kitchen Clients Ask Before We Start
Will you handle the City of Auburn permits for my kitchen?
Yes. Any kitchen work that touches plumbing, electrical, gas, or structure gets permitted through the Auburn Permit Center. We file the application, schedule every inspection, and carry the code compliance so you're never standing in line at the city.
How many weeks does an Auburn kitchen remodel take?
Most Auburn kitchens are 4 to 8 weeks of active construction after demo. A cabinet-and-counter refresh can wrap in 2–3 weeks, while a full gut with a new layout usually runs 8–12 weeks, plus 2–4 weeks of design and permitting up front. You'll have a week-by-week schedule before we start.
How much should I budget for a kitchen remodel in Auburn?
Auburn kitchens typically land between $20,000 and $65,000. A mid-range job — semi-custom cabinets, quartz counters, updated lighting — usually falls around $32,000–$50,000, while custom cabinetry, premium appliances, and moving walls push higher. Every estimate is itemized line by line.
Do you take kitchen jobs in Lakeland Hills and Lea Hill?
Constantly. Those two neighborhoods, plus downtown and North Auburn, are regular territory for us. It's a 12–15 minute drive from our Kent base up Highway 167 or West Valley Highway, so measuring, delivering, and meeting inspectors across Auburn is part of a normal week.
Are you licensed, bonded, and insured in Washington?
Yes. Big Build Construction holds full Washington State licensing, bonding, and insurance, and that covers all of our Auburn work. Everything is built to code and inspected wherever the city calls for it.
Can the kitchen be finished before Auburn schools go back?
Usually, yes. We often build Auburn kitchen remodels around the Auburn School District calendar — demo in early summer, kitchen handed back a couple of weeks before classes resume. Tell us your hard deadline and we schedule the whole job backward from it.
Which layouts do you handle in older Auburn ranches?
From opening the wall between a Lea Hill kitchen and family room to reworking a cramped downtown ranch galley. In 1950s–1970s Auburn homes that often means updating undersized plumbing and 2-wire feeds behind the range as part of the remodel.
Can you add an island with a sink and outlets?
Yes. An island sink, dishwasher, or added outlets means new supply, drain, and circuit runs — all permitted and inspected. In older Auburn homes we'll often upgrade the panel or replace outdated wiring at the same time so the new island is safe and to code.
Do you replace builder-grade kitchens in Lakeland Hills?
That's one of our most common Lakeland Hills jobs. The 1990s–2000s homes there have solid bones, so the work is swapping builder-grade cabinets, laminate, and lighting for quartz, real cabinetry, and modern fixtures rather than fixing systems.
